# Set B — optional mixed practice
If useful, try 50 minutes: 5 reading, 40 working and 5 checking. You can also work at your own pace. This set focuses on different content from Set A; compare what you can explain rather than counting completed questions. Try the questions before reading the explanations. It can fit Week 16 lesson 1.
B1: Given RoomSession.remaining initially 1 and reserve implemented as `if self.remaining < 0: raise ValueError("Full")` then `self.remaining -= 1`; OnlineSession inherits and overrides location->"Online", RoomSession.location->"Room". State output of a location-call loop on one of each, explain polymorphic dispatch, repair the reservation condition, specify test exposing the original fault and expected corrected behaviour.
B2: A report INNER JOINs Resource to Loan and uses COUNT(*). Requirement is ALL resources, total loans and active loans (actual Loan row with NULL ReturnDate). Identify missing-zero-row fault, repair join/link, explain active count avoiding outer placeholder, predict total/active pairs. SQL expression allowed: COUNT(CASE WHEN l.ReturnDate IS NULL THEN l.LoanID END).
B3: Write summarise(rows)->dictionary accumulating exact topic counts. Criteria: initialise/iterate/unpack, enforce topic non-empty string, enforce non-negative exact integer excluding bool, repeated/first-key accumulation, return correct mapping including empty list, meaningful repeated/zero/invalid tests with expected outcomes. Do not mutate input. Contract assumes each row is a pair; no live input interface required.
B4: A flat loan sheet contains LoanID,ResourceID,ResourceLabel,CategoryID,CategoryName,MemberID,MemberName,StartDate,ReturnDate. Dependencies: LoanID->ResourceID,MemberID,dates;ResourceID->Label,CategoryID;CategoryID->Name;MemberID->Name. Explain two transitive dependencies, decompose into Category/Resource/Member/Loan with PK/FKs, justify LoanID rather than ResourceID+MemberID for repeated events and relationships, explain explicit rollback after a second-step domain error, and justify retention/recovery decisions with needed evidence rather than automatic deletion. Inspection is separately supplied; doesn't arise from this flat sheet.
Use commands and source facts precisely. Note uncertainty, compare explanations, then retry with changed data.
